correctness.rationale: Submodularity makes adjoining a rank-zero line rank-preserving. For any nonloop secret S there is a rank-two plane through S: otherwise the induction on sums of two hyperplanes containing S in RESULT.md propagates rank one to E. Such a plane supplies a nonreconstructing line in every complement to S. If the matroid has a loop L, the rank-one plane S+L has a nonloop line other than S and L (its intersection with the loop subspace is exactly L); choose a complement of S containing that line to obtain a reconstructing line as well. In the loop-free nonuniform case, choose S in a rank-one plane; its intersection with any complement supplies a reconstructing line. Either yields two lines with different reconstruction behavior in one port, impossible for any integer dimension threshold, including an empty port. In the uniform case adjoining S increases dimension by one and increases rank exactly at dimensions zero and one, giving threshold two.
residual_risks: This is a symbolic rank-axiom check, not a Lean proof or expert attestation; no computation is required.

value.rationale: It settles a natural first nontrivial rank of a documented classification question. It shows exactly when threshold access survives every choice of secret line and complement, using a mixed-line obstruction that detects both loops and dependent planes. This is a structural converse, not another example of the known sufficient condition.
residual_risks: The result concerns all ports jointly and gives no classification for a single port, higher rank, or near-threshold behavior.
